text: In the morning, when you rise unwillingly, let this thought be present: I am rising to the work of a human being.
Begin the morning by saying to yourself: I shall meet with the busybody, the ungrateful, the arrogant. But none of them can harm me, and I cannot be angry with my kin.
Do every act of your life as if it were the last, with simple dignity, and you will give yourself relief from all other thoughts.
Nowhere can a person retire with more quiet or more freedom from trouble than into their own soul.
Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
Do not be disgusted, discouraged or dissatisfied if you do not succeed in doing everything according to right principles. When you have failed, return back again.
When circumstances have disturbed you, quickly return to yourself. You will have more mastery over the harmony by continually returning to it.
Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will always bubble up, if you will always dig.
Do not disturb yourself by thinking of the whole of your life. On every occasion ask yourself: what is there in this that is unbearable?
No longer talk at all about the kind of person a good person ought to be, but be such.
Be like the promontory against which the waves continually break; it stands firm and tames the fury of the water around it.
Such as are your habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of your mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.
The perfection of character is this: to live each day as if it were the last, without frenzy, without apathy, without pretence.
If you are pained by any external thing, it is not the thing that disturbs you, but your own judgement about it. And it is in your power to wipe out that judgement now.
Every person lives only this present moment, which is an indivisible point. The rest of life is either past or uncertain.
Let it make no difference to you whether you are cold or warm, drowsy or rested, if you are doing your duty.
Do not let future things disturb you. You will come to them, if you must, with the same reason you now use for present things.
Occupy yourself with few things, says the philosopher, if you would be tranquil.
How much trouble a person avoids who does not look to what a neighbour says or does, but only to what they do themselves.
You must build your life action by action, and be content if each act does its duty as far as possible.
If a thing is difficult for you to accomplish, do not think it impossible for anyone. If it is possible for a human being, think that it can be attained by you too.
Take away your opinion, and the complaint 'I have been harmed' is taken away. Take away the complaint, and the harm is taken away.
The mind that is free from passions is a citadel; a person has nothing more secure to fly to for refuge.
Wipe out the imagination. Stop the pulling of the strings. Confine yourself to the present.
Every habit and faculty is maintained and increased by the corresponding actions: the habit of walking by walking, the habit of running by running.
If you would be a good reader, read; if a writer, write.
Whatever you would make habitual, practise it; and if you would not make a thing habitual, do not practise it, but accustom yourself to something else.
No great thing is created suddenly, any more than a bunch of grapes or a fig. If you tell me you want a fig, I answer that there must be time. Let it first blossom, then bear fruit, then ripen.
Some things are in our control and others are not.
People are disturbed not by things, but by the opinions they hold about things.
From this moment, consider yourself worthy of living as a grown person who is making progress, and let whatever seems best be a law you will not break.
First say to yourself what you would be; then do what you have to do.
Prescribe some character and form of conduct for yourself, which you will keep both when alone and in company.
It is difficulties that show what people are.
With every accident that befalls you, turn to yourself and ask what power you have for putting it to use.
In every affair consider what comes before and what follows, and then undertake it.
No one is free who is not master of himself.
Hold every hour in your grasp. Lay hold of today's task, and you will not need to depend so much on tomorrow's.
While we are postponing, life speeds by.
Nothing is ours except time.
What bad habit have I cured today? What fault have I resisted? In what respect am I better?
The mind should be called to account every day.
Philosophy teaches us to act, not to speak.
Everywhere means nowhere.
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
When a person does not know what harbour they are making for, no wind is the right wind.
Let us go to our sleep with joy and gladness; let us say: I have lived.
Every day ought to be regulated as if it closed the series and rounded out our existence.
As long as you live, keep learning how to live.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste much of it.
cite: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life 1

text: The greatest obstacle to living is expectancy, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today.
cite: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life 9

text: It is not the one who has too little who is poor, but the one who craves more.
Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
To live is to be a soldier.
Persist, and strengthen yourself daily, until what is now a good impulse becomes a settled habit of good.
Each day, gather something that will fortify you, and after running over many thoughts, choose one to digest that day.
Set aside a few days in which you are content with the plainest fare, and ask yourself: is this the condition I feared?
There are more things likely to frighten us than to crush us.
Fire tests gold; misfortune tests the brave.
The mind must be given rest; it will rise better and keener after it.
Withdraw into yourself as far as you can.
Virtue is not only theoretical knowledge; it is practical application as well.
If you do something good with labour, the labour passes and the good remains. If you do something shameful for pleasure, the pleasure passes and the shame remains.
Well-being is attained by small steps, yet it is no small thing.
cite: Zeno of Citium, in Diogenes Laertius 7.26

text: You have a right to your actions, but never to their fruits. Let the fruit not be your motive, and do not cling to inaction.
original:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
transliteration:
karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi

text: Steady in yoga, do your work and let go of attachment, the same in success and failure. This evenness is called yoga.
original:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
transliteration:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga ucyate

text: On this path no effort is ever lost, and no harm is ever done. Even a little of this practice protects from great fear.
original:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते ।
स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
transliteration:
nehābhikrama-nāśo 'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpam apy asya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt

text: Lift yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. The self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is its enemy.
original:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
transliteration:
uddhared ātmanātmānaṁ nātmānam avasādayet
ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ

text: Without doubt the mind is restless and hard to hold. But it is held by practice and by detachment.
original:
असंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलम् ।
अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
transliteration:
asaṁśayaṁ mahā-bāho mano durnigrahaṁ calam
abhyāsena tu kaunteya vairāgyeṇa ca gṛhyate

text: For one who is measured in eating and rest, measured in effort, measured in sleep and waking, yoga destroys sorrow.
original:
युक्ताहारविहारस्य युक्तचेष्टस्य कर्मसु ।
युक्तस्वप्नावबोधस्य योगो भवति दुःखहा ॥
transliteration:
yuktāhāra-vihārasya yukta-ceṣṭasya karmasu
yukta-svapnāvabodhasya yogo bhavati duḥkha-hā

text: Neither here nor hereafter is there ruin for such a one. No one who does good, my friend, ever comes to a bad end.
original:
पार्थ नैवेह नामुत्र विनाशस्तस्य विद्यते ।
न हि कल्याणकृत्कश्चिद्दुर्गतिं तात गच्छति ॥
transliteration:
pārtha naiveha nāmutra vināśas tasya vidyate
na hi kalyāṇa-kṛt kaścid durgatiṁ tāta gacchati

text: Do the work that is yours to do, for action is better than inaction.
original: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
transliteration: niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hy akarmaṇaḥ

text: Whatever the best person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world pursues.
original:
यद्यदाचरति श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जनः ।
स यत्प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
transliteration:
yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhas tat tad evetaro janaḥ
sa yat pramāṇaṁ kurute lokas tad anuvartate

text: Better your own path done imperfectly than another's path done well.
original: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
transliteration: śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ para-dharmāt sv-anuṣṭhitāt

text: One who acts without attachment, offering every action to the Divine, is untouched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is untouched by water.
original:
ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः ।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा ॥
transliteration:
brahmaṇy ādhāya karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā karoti yaḥ
lipyate na sa pāpena padma-patram ivāmbhasā

text: The touch of the senses brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently.
original:
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौन्तेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः ।
आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत ॥
transliteration:
mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ
āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata

text: Brooding on objects of the senses, attachment to them grows. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
original:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते ।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥
transliteration:
dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate
saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate

text: As rivers flow into the ocean, which is ever filled yet stays still, so the one into whom desires flow finds peace, not the one who chases desires.
original:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ।
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam acala-pratiṣṭhaṁ samudram āpaḥ praviśanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśanti sarve sa śāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī

text: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there draw it back and rest it in the self.
original:
यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् ।
ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
transliteration:
yato yato niścarati manaś cañcalam asthiram
tatas tato niyamyaitad ātmany eva vaśaṁ nayet

text: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker: that is the image of the yogi whose mind is disciplined.
original:
यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता ।
योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ॥
transliteration:
yathā dīpo nivāta-stho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā
yogino yata-cittasya yuñjato yogam ātmanaḥ

text: If you cannot hold your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me through the yoga of practice.
original:
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् ।
अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥
transliteration:
atha cittaṁ samādhātuṁ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram
abhyāsa-yogena tato mām icchāptuṁ dhanañjaya

text: That which is like poison at first and like nectar in the end, born of a clear mind, is called the happiness of goodness.
original:
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम् ॥
transliteration:
yat tad agre viṣam iva pariṇāme 'mṛtopamam
tat sukhaṁ sāttvikaṁ proktam ātma-buddhi-prasāda-jam

text: That which comes from the senses meeting their objects, like nectar at first and like poison in the end, is called the happiness of passion.
original:
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
transliteration:
viṣayendriya-saṁyogād yat tad agre 'mṛtopamam
pariṇāme viṣam iva tat sukhaṁ rājasaṁ smṛtam

text: Yoga is skill in action.
original: योगः कर्मसु कौशलम् ।
transliteration: yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam

text: So, without attachment, always do the work that must be done. By working without attachment, one reaches the highest.
original:
तस्मादसक्तः सततं कार्यं कर्म समाचर ।
असक्तो ह्याचरन्कर्म परमाप्नोति पूरुषः ॥
transliteration:
tasmād asaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samācara
asakto hy ācaran karma param āpnoti pūruṣaḥ

text: For one who has conquered the mind, the mind is the best of friends. For one who has not, it behaves like an enemy.
original:
बन्धुरात्मात्मनस्तस्य येनात्मैवात्मना जितः ।
अनात्मनस्तु शत्रुत्वे वर्तेतात्मैव शत्रुवत् ॥
transliteration:
bandhur ātmātmanas tasya yenātmaivātmanā jitaḥ
anātmanas tu śatrutve vartetātmaiva śatru-vat

text: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give, whatever discipline you keep, do it as an offering to me.
original:
यत्करोषि यदश्नासि यज्जुहोषि ददासि यत् ।
यत्तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत्कुरुष्व मदर्पणम् ॥
transliteration:
yat karoṣi yad aśnāsi yaj juhoṣi dadāsi yat
yat tapasyasi kaunteya tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam

text: Treat alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, and then take up the work.
original:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ ।
ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
transliteration:
sukha-duḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi

text: Do not yield to weakness; it does not become you. Cast off this small faint-heartedness and arise.
original:
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
transliteration:
klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitat tvayy upapadyate
kṣudraṁ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa

text: One who does the work that ought to be done, without depending on its fruit, is a true renunciate and a true yogi.
original:
अनाश्रितः कर्मफलं कार्यं कर्म करोति यः ।
स संन्यासी च योगी च न निरग्निर्न चाक्रियः ॥
transliteration:
anāśritaḥ karma-phalaṁ kāryaṁ karma karoti yaḥ
sa sannyāsī ca yogī ca na niragnir na cākriyaḥ

text: This yoga should be practised with determination and a mind that does not lose heart.
original: स निश्चयेन योक्तव्यो योगोऽनिर्विण्णचेतसा ।
transliteration: sa niścayena yoktavyo yogo 'nirviṇṇa-cetasā

text: Little by little, let one become still, with the intellect held by steadiness.
original: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद्बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया ।
transliteration: śanaiḥ śanair uparamed buddhyā dhṛti-gṛhītayā

text: It is desire, it is anger, born of restless passion, all-devouring. Know it as the enemy here.
original:
काम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः ।
महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
transliteration:
kāma eṣa krodha eṣa rajo-guṇa-samudbhavaḥ
mahāśano mahā-pāpmā viddhy enam iha vairiṇam

text: Desire, anger and greed are the threefold gate to the ruin of the self. Therefore let them go.
original:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
transliteration:
tri-vidhaṁ narakasyedaṁ dvāraṁ nāśanam ātmanaḥ
kāmaḥ krodhas tathā lobhas tasmād etat trayaṁ tyajet

text: Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of heart: this is called the discipline of the mind.
original:
मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते ॥
transliteration:
manaḥ-prasādaḥ saumyatvaṁ maunam ātma-vinigrahaḥ
bhāva-saṁśuddhir ity etat tapo mānasam ucyate

text: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love I accept.
original:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति ।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
transliteration:
patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati
tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ

text: Do not abandon the work that is yours, even if it has flaws. Every undertaking is clouded by some flaw, as fire is by smoke.
original:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः ॥
transliteration:
saha-jaṁ karma kaunteya sa-doṣam api na tyajet
sarvārambhā hi doṣeṇa dhūmenāgnir ivāvṛtāḥ

text: Better than practice is knowledge; better than knowledge is meditation; better than meditation is letting go of the fruits of action. Peace follows at once.
Arise, awake, and learn by going to the wise. Sharp as the edge of a razor and hard to cross is that path, say the sages.
original:
उत्तिष्ठत जाग्रत प्राप्य वरान्निबोधत ।
क्षुरस्य धारा निशिता दुरत्यया दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति ॥
transliteration:
uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata
kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṁ pathas tat kavayo vadanti

text: The good and the pleasant both come to a person. The wise choose the good over the pleasant; the foolish choose the pleasant.
original:
श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीरः ।
श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद्वृणीते ॥
transliteration:
śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau samparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ
śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yoga-kṣemād vṛṇīte

text: Know the self as the rider in a chariot and the body as the chariot. Know the intellect as the charioteer and the mind as the reins.
original:
आत्मानं रथिनं विद्धि शरीरं रथमेव तु ।
बुद्धिं तु सारथिं विद्धि मनः प्रग्रहमेव च ॥
transliteration:
ātmānaṁ rathinaṁ viddhi śarīraṁ ratham eva tu
buddhiṁ tu sārathiṁ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca

text: As a person acts, so they become. As is their desire, so is their resolve; as is their resolve, so is their deed; and whatever deed they do, that they become.
original: यथाकारी यथाचारी तथा भवति ।
transliteration: yathākārī yathācārī tathā bhavati

text: Lead me from the unreal to the real. Lead me from darkness to light. Lead me from death to immortality.
original:
असतो मा सद्गमय ।
तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय ।
मृत्योर्माऽमृतं गमय ॥
transliteration:
asato mā sad gamaya
tamaso mā jyotir gamaya
mṛtyor māmṛtaṁ gamaya

text: Truth alone triumphs.
original: सत्यमेव जयते ।
transliteration: satyam eva jayate

text: Doing your work here, wish to live a hundred years.
original: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतं समाः ।
transliteration: kurvann eveha karmāṇi jijīviṣec chataṁ samāḥ

text: Speak the truth. Walk in dharma. Do not neglect your own study.
original: सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः ।
transliteration: satyaṁ vada, dharmaṁ cara, svādhyāyān mā pramadaḥ

text: May my mind be of auspicious resolve.
original: तन्मे मनः शिवसङ्कल्पमस्तु ।
transliteration: tan me manaḥ śiva-saṅkalpam astu

text: Let noble thoughts come to us from every side.
original: आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतः ।
transliteration: ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvataḥ

text: The movements of the mind are stilled by practice and non-attachment.
original: अभ्यासवैराग्याभ्यां तन्निरोधः ।
transliteration: abhyāsa-vairāgyābhyāṁ tan-nirodhaḥ

text: Practice is the effort to stay steady in that stillness.
original: तत्र स्थितौ यत्नोऽभ्यासः ।
transliteration: tatra sthitau yatno 'bhyāsaḥ

text: Practice becomes firmly grounded when it is kept up for a long time, without break, and with devotion.
original: स तु दीर्घकालनैरन्तर्यसत्कारासेवितो दृढभूमिः ।
transliteration: sa tu dīrgha-kāla-nairantarya-satkārāsevito dṛḍha-bhūmiḥ

text: Discipline, self-study and surrender to the Divine make up the yoga of action.
original: तपःस्वाध्यायेश्वरप्रणिधानानि क्रियायोगः ।
transliteration: tapaḥ-svādhyāyeśvara-praṇidhānāni kriyā-yogaḥ

text: When disturbed by unwholesome thoughts, cultivate their opposite.
original: वितर्कबाधने प्रतिपक्षभावनम् ।
transliteration: vitarka-bādhane pratipakṣa-bhāvanam

text: Posture should be steady and easeful.
original: स्थिरसुखमासनम् ।
transliteration: sthira-sukham āsanam

text: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
cite: Swami Vivekananda, Lectures from Colombo to Almora

text: Take up one idea. Make that one idea your life; think of it, dream of it, live on that idea. This is the way to success.
The world is a grand moral gymnasium, where we all have to take exercise so as to become stronger and stronger.
We are what our thoughts have made us; so take care about what you think. Words are secondary. Thoughts live; they travel far.
Dharma protects those who protect it.
original: धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः ।
transliteration: dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ

text: Tasks are accomplished by effort, not by wishing. Deer do not walk into the mouth of a sleeping lion.
original:
उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः ।
न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः ॥
transliteration:
udyamena hi sidhyanti kāryāṇi na manorathaiḥ
na hi suptasya siṁhasya praviśanti mukhe mṛgāḥ

text: Drop by drop, the pot is filled. So it is with all learning, with virtue and with wealth.
original:
जलबिन्दुनिपातेन क्रमशः पूर्यते घटः ।
स हेतुः सर्वविद्यानां धर्मस्य च धनस्य च ॥
transliteration:
jala-bindu-nipātena kramaśaḥ pūryate ghaṭaḥ
sa hetuḥ sarva-vidyānāṁ dharmasya ca dhanasya ca

text: What you would do tomorrow, do today; what you would do today, do now. The moment may pass, and when will you do it then?
original:
काल करे सो आज कर, आज करे सो अब ।
पल में परलय होएगी, बहुरि करेगा कब ॥
transliteration:
kāl kare so āj kar, āj kare so ab
pal meṁ paralay hoegī, bahuri karegā kab

text: Slowly, slowly, O mind; everything happens in its own time. The gardener may pour a hundred pots of water, but fruit comes only in its season.
original:
धीरे-धीरे रे मना, धीरे सब कुछ होय ।
माली सींचे सौ घड़ा, ऋतु आए फल होय ॥
transliteration:
dhīre-dhīre re manā, dhīre sab kuch hoy
mālī sīṁce sau ghaṛā, ṛtu āe phal hoy

text: The lowest never begin, for fear of obstacles. The middling begin, but stop when obstacles come. The best, struck down by obstacles again and again, never give up what they have begun.
original:
प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः
प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ।
विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः
प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति ॥
transliteration:
prārabhyate na khalu vighna-bhayena nīcaiḥ
prārabhya vighna-vihatā viramanti madhyāḥ
vighnaiḥ punaḥ punar api pratihanyamānāḥ
prārabdham uttama-janā na parityajanti
